verdict.line: You lose if Irelia hits 5 Ionian Fervor stacks and dives behind a charged Defiant Dance (W) before you can punish her cooldowns; you win if you poke her down with Test of Spirit (E) before level 6 and grind her out with tentacle sustain once Q (Bladesurge) and E (Flawless Duet) are both on cooldown.

brief.thesis: Irelia's Ionian Fervor passive turns extended fights in her favor once she's stacked, but she has no reliable gap-close or stun before her E (Flawless Duet) comes online, while your E (Test of Spirit) outranges everything she has at 900. The 52.7% win rate over 581 games reflects a lane that's even on paper but structurally favors whoever controls engagement: you win by poking from range and fighting on your tentacle terrain, she wins by closing distance already stacked.

theirWindow.when: Irelia at 5 stacks with W ready
theirWindow.what: At max passive stacks she gains bonus on-hit damage, and Defiant Dance (W) reduces the physical damage she takes while charging. Do not stand and trade autos into a charging W at full stacks; disengage or bait the charge with Tentacle Smash (Q) first.

yourWindow.when: Her Q and E both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Without Bladesurge (Q, 10/9/8/7/6s) to gap-close or reset and without Flawless Duet (E, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) to stun you, Irelia cannot threaten an all-in. Leap in with Harsh Lesson (W) into Test of Spirit (E) for a free trade.

start.why: Best measured start into this matchup (56.1% over 412 games) — the extra AD and sustain let you win E pokes and healing-potion through her early Q trades.

boots.why: Reduces incoming basic attack damage, directly undercutting the bonus on-hit damage Irelia gets from Ionian Fervor at 5 stacks.

core.why: Highest win-rate opening item (69.4% in this build path) — the slow on-hit punishes her for standing in melee range after a Q dash.
Shred stacks make your W-E leap combos and tentacle swings hit harder in extended trades.
The HP and damage-reduction shield lets you survive her stacked-passive all-in window at levels 6-10 and keep fighting.

runes.keystoneWhy: Grasp heals you and grows your max HP on every poke trade, stacking with your passive Tentacle healing so you win the attrition war even when Irelia lands a Q reset.

summoners.why: Exhaust directly neuters her 5-stack Ionian Fervor burst and slows her Q-engage follow-up, the measured 53.1% win-rate combo for this matchup.

playing.title: Poke with E before level 6
playing.detail: Use Test of Spirit (E, 900 range) to chip Irelia from max range — she has no stun and no ultimate yet, so she can't punish the poke.

playing.title: Track her passive stack count
playing.detail: Back off trades once she nears 5 Ionian Fervor stacks unless you have Harsh Lesson (W) ready to burst in and retreat immediately.

playing.title: Don't commit into a charging W
playing.detail: Defiant Dance reduces her physical damage taken while charging (20/18/16/14/12s cooldown); bait it out with Tentacle Smash (Q) before committing your full combo.

playing.title: Punish missing Q and E
playing.detail: When both her dash and her stun are down, Irelia has no way to engage or escape — this is your window to leap in.

playing.title: Fight near terrain for tentacles
playing.detail: Your passive spawns Tentacles on nearby impassible terrain, so pull fights toward walls and jungle entrances so Q and R have tentacles to activate.

playing.title: Save R for her all-in
playing.detail: Hold Leap of Faith (120/95/70s cooldown) until she commits her Bladesurge dash into you, so the tentacles it spawns swing for the whole fight.

playing.title: Buy Steelcaps on your first boots
playing.detail: Plated Steelcaps cuts the on-hit damage spike she gets at max passive stacks, which is her primary win condition.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoner numbers are measured from live games on the current patch via OP.GG; the matchup reasoning and timing calls are my own tactical read.

stats.opponentTip: Even though Illaoi is strong in melee fights, an Irelia with 5 stacks of (P) flips the odds in her favor. Try to harass Irelia through [E] without allowing her to close in before reaching level 6, and engage with [E]-[R] if Irelia closes in after reaching level 6.
